name: Mexican red knee

popularity.src: https://www.thetarantulacollective.com/caresheets/brachypelma-hamorii (classic beginner species, stocked by every dealer and chains; judged, not measured)

diet: Crickets, roaches; adult 4-5 large crickets or 1 large dubia every 2-3 weeks

fast_tolerance_days.src: https://www.thetarantulacollective.com/caresheets/brachypelma-hamorii

molt_note: Wait 5-10 days after an adult molt before feeding; fangs must be solid black and exoskeleton hard (TTC). Refuses food and hides/webs shut before molt.
venom_handling: Venom not medically significant; urticating hairs kicked from abdomen cause irritation; fang puncture can get infected (Wikipedia). Docile.
colour: Body black (adult male upper abdomen black; female carapace mainly black with brownish-pink border or pale orange-yellow starburst). Legs black to reddish-black with the signature bright orange knee (patella base deep orange, rest of patella and lower tibia pale orange-yellow, metatarsus tips yellowish-white). Sources: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brachypelma_hamorii and https://www.thetarantulacollective.com/caresheets/brachypelma-hamorii (vivid black with bright orange markings on legs).
notes: Fetched: TTC care sheet, Wikipedia. Humidity only "moderate" on TTC (no %), so range is assumption. Floor = 3x leg span long, half that wide (derived from TTC rule 3-4x leg span; no height given, 15 cm assumed). Lifespan 25-30 yr female TTC, 30 Wikipedia. Prices from search-result text of retailer pages, not full fetches.

name: Chilean rose

popularity.src: https://www.thetarantulacollective.com/caresheets/grammostola-rosea (long-standing top beginner species at pet chains; judged)

venom_handling: Venom mild; Type III urticating hairs flicked when startled; mood swings docile to defensive.
colour: Red colour form: warm brown-pink to rosy carapace and legs with pinkish hairs over a darker base; the grey form (now often G. porteri) is cooler, muted grey-brown. TTC: pinkish hues often seen on the carapace. Sources: https://www.thetarantulacollective.com/caresheets/grammostola-rosea and https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammostola_rosea (colour morph names only, no full description).
notes: Fetched: TTC, Wikipedia. Leg span 15 cm (TTC); body length not on either page (assumption). Temp: TTC 20-23 C ambient, Wikipedia says keepers use 25-30 C; used 20-25. No humidity % given (dry upland desert origin); assumption.

name: Orchid mantis
diet: Live flying insects (house/blue bottle flies, small moths), supplemented with small crickets/locusts; fruit flies for early nymphs; mist for drink.
molt_note: Hangs upside down from mesh to molt; ventilation matters as much as humidity; do not disturb or feed during molt.
venom_handling: Not venomous; delicate, do not handle.
colour: Female: semi-translucent white body with pink (or yellow/orange/green/brown) accents; fin-like petal lobes on the walking legs, pink-white; green 'necklace' mark on neck and sometimes a green spot on the back. Male: smaller, more orange-toned, brownish spot on back, brown-red neck mark. Nymph: pink and white with semi-opalescent flattened limbs and a small black spot at abdomen tip (Wikipedia, IK, Swell UK pages).
behaviors: sway like a petal in wind
notes: Round 2: numbers from insectkeeper, Swell UK, Wikipedia, BugsInCyberspace pages. Sources disagree: lifespan 5-9 months, temp 25-35 C day (night min 18 C), size female 6-7 cm. Popularity 4 is a judgement (several US retailers stock it at $50-65; not a measured best-seller rank). Price low $50 fetched from Bugs in Cyberspace (2nd-3rd instar, out of stock); typical/hi are round-1 snippet prices, retailer pages returned 429/410 this pass. Substrate irrelevant (mesh climber); 20 mm assumed.

name: Ghost mantis
diet: Flies (fruit flies for newborns), small moths, small crickets; prey about head-sized; feed when abdomen looks thin.
molt_note: Hangs upside down to molt; low humidity can strand it in old skin; colour can change drastically between molts.
venom_handling: Not venomous; adult females play dead when threatened (thanatosis).
colour: Dead-leaf mimic: usually dark brown, also sand, light brown, reddish brown or greenish grey (green more likely in humid conditions); forewings look like a dried leaf with pigment 'creases'; leaf-like lobes on legs and an elongated crest on the head. First/second instar nymphs dark (ant mimics). Males have transparent wings longer than the abdomen (Wikipedia, keepinginsects pages).
notes: Round 2: keepinginsects, jackofallinverts, Wikipedia, BugsInCyberspace pages fetched (dubiaroaches/reptilesupply returned 429). Humidity conflicts: jackofallinverts 35-50%, keepinginsects 60-90%; stored 50-70 as derived compromise (round-1 dubiaroaches figure). Lifespan jackofallinverts: females 6-8 mo after adult molt, males 2-4 mo. Popularity 4 assumed (widely stocked). Price: $19 unsexed L2/L3 fetched (out of stock); hi $36 from Mantisplace search snippet only.

name: Chinese mantis
diet: Flies, crickets, moths; adults take larger prey.
molt_note: Hangs to molt, needs height.
venom_handling: Not venomous; pinches.
colour: Green or brown with a green stripe along the wing margin; long slender body (assumption from general knowledge).
notes: Popularity 4: Josh's Frogs sells captive-bred ones. Adults ~100 mm (4 in), up to 125; 22-30 C; 50-70% RH; 8-12 month life. Price is an assumption (not found on a retailer page this pass).

name: Spiny flower mantis
diet: Flies and small moths (not large prey like adult locusts); adults every few days, nymphs daily; mist for drink.
molt_note: Hangs upside down to molt; prone to mould/fungus so ventilation is critical; keep on the dry side.
group_rule: solitary (nymphs to L4 can share; cannibalistic later), 1 per enclosure
venom_handling: Not venomous.
colour: Adult: mostly white with bright green stripes/accents on legs and orange-green stripes on body (Wikipedia: typically light green, also yellow, pink or red); eyes lilac to deep purple; forewings carry a black, green and cream eyespot ringed by a green patch; inner hind wings bright orange-yellow, outer hind wings transparent. Nymphs black until L3, then orange-pink spots fading to white each molt.
notes: Round 2: insectkeeper, keepinginsects, Wikipedia fetched. Size conflict: Wikipedia 40 mm, insectkeeper 1.5 in, keepinginsects '4-5 in' (unit unclear, rejected). Humidity: insectkeeper 40-60%, keepinginsects ~60% (stored 40-60). Temp 25-30 C (keepinginsects), insectkeeper ~27 C. Lifespan insectkeeper ~6 mo, up to 1 yr. Popularity 4 assumed. Price NOT found on a fetched retailer page (usmantis/tydye returned 429): assumption.

name: Indian / laboratory stick insect
diet: Privet (staple), bramble, ivy, hawthorn, rose, raspberry, oak, hazel; mist leaves for water; feeds at night.
molt_note: Hangs upside down to molt; cage height ~25 cm+ needed; may drop legs.
group_rule: colony, 5-10 per 25 cm cage (all female, parthenogenetic; ~1 in 1000 male)
venom_handling: Harmless; feigns death when disturbed.
colour: Wingless thin twig body. Bright green in young or humid, well-lit conditions; brown, tan or grey-green when drier/darker, shifting across molts. Adult females: light green to dark brown with red patches at the base of the forelegs and yellow patches on the mid-legs (Wikipedia, FurryCritter, Bug Pets pages). Males thin and brown.
notes: Round 2: Wikipedia, PSG species page (female 80 mm, male 55 mm, 'very easy'), FurryCritter, Bug Pets (UK) fetched; dubiaroaches/reptilesupply 429. Popularity 5 assumed (classic pet/school insect; no ranking page). Temp 18-25 C (FurryCritter) vs lab 23 C (round 1 JoVE snippet; page fetch empty). Price is UK retailer: GBP 12.99 for 5 nymphs (out of stock) = GBP 2.60 each, converted at 1.30 USD/GBP (derived); lo/hi assumptions.

name: Vietnamese / Annam walking stick
diet: Bramble (blackberry/raspberry), hawthorn, oak, rose, red maple; mist foliage.
molt_note: Hangs to molt; height at least 3x body length; legs regrow.
group_rule: colony, several adults per 30x30x45 cm (mostly parthenogenetic)
venom_handling: Harmless.
colour: Wingless, slim twig-like. Nymphs hatch light tan/beige, often turning green during early molts; adults usually brown from light tan to dark chocolate or golden brown, some stay green (FurryCritter, Wikipedia, Bug Pets pages). Eggs mottled black and white.
notes: Round 2: FurryCritter species page, PSG (female 110 mm, male 75 mm), Wikipedia (100-120 mm, 5-7 months), Bug Pets UK fetched; dubiaroaches/arent.pl blocked. Lifespan conflicts: 5-7 months (Wikipedia, FurryCritter, Bug Pets) vs 12-18 months (FurryCritter article page, German sheet ~12). Humidity 50-60% (FurryCritter) vs 60-80% (Polish round-1 snippet). Enclosure: FurryCritter 12x12x18 in (30x30x45 cm). Popularity 4 assumed. Price UK Bug Pets: GBP 14.99 for 2 = GBP 7.50 each, x1.30 = $9.75 (derived); lo/hi assumptions.

name: Giant prickly stick insect
diet: Bramble, raspberry, oak, rose, hazel, eucalyptus (may colour/size less on non-eucalyptus); mist leaves for water; nocturnal.
molt_note: Hangs to molt; ventilation very important; nymphs molt best near 60% RH; eucalyptus can mould in moist cages.
group_rule: colony ok, 3-6 per 30x30x45 cm; one male + one female for breeding
venom_handling: Harmless; spines scratchy.
colour: Highly variable: usually light to mid brown, also green, beige, dark brown, reddish, cream or white. Female: thorn-like spikes over the body incl. a tuft on the head, lobed leaf-like legs, tiny non-functional wings, curled tail held over the back; male: slim, brown with dark brown specks, long wings, thorns only around the face. Rare lichen-coloured young females (Wikipedia, keepinginsects, Bug Pets pages).
notes: Round 2: Wikipedia (female 20 cm incl. legs/ ~18 mo; male 11 cm, 6-8 mo), keepinginsects (female ~15 cm body; 20-30 C), Bug Pets UK (20-25 C, 60% RH, GBP 13.99) fetched; dubiaroaches/reptilesupply 429 (round-1 snippet figures 20-28 C, 50-70% RH kept as reference). name: Giant vinegaroon
diet: Crickets, roaches, worms; 1-3 prey items; weekly (Tye Dye Iguana) to every 3-4 weeks (Tarantula Collective); may refuse when full; wait a week after molt.
molt_note: Seals into burrow to molt; no feeding until hard (5-7 days slings, 7-10 days juveniles, at least a week adults).
venom_handling: Not venomous; seldom pinches; sprays ~85% acetic acid from tail base that stings eyes/mucous membranes, so wash hands.
colour: Body typically black (Bugs in Cyberspace photo caption), with some sections and appendages brown or reddish-brown (Animal Diversity Web); Texas animals slightly lighter brown, Arizona larger and darker (Tarantula Collective). Flat oval carapace and abdomen, two heavy pincer pedipalps, a long thin flexible whip tail, one pair of long sensory front legs held forward, six walking legs.
notes: Round 2: Tye Dye Iguana, Tarantula Collective, Animal Diversity Web, Wikipedia, Bugs in Cyberspace pages fetched. Size conflicts: ADW/Wikipedia 40-60 mm body excl. tail; Tarantula Collective 10 cm body; Tye Dye 4-6 in; BIC 2.75-3 in with pedipalps; stored 75 mm as a derived middle. Lifespan: females up to 20 yr, males 5-10 (Tye Dye/TC); ADW 4-7 wild; stored 10. Humidity 70-80% only on Tye Dye (TC gives none). Feed interval conflicts 7 d vs 21-28 d. Popularity 4 assumed.
